{{DISPLAYTITLE:''p''-adic distribution}}
In mathematics, a '''p-adic distribution''' is an analogue of ordinary [[distribution (mathematics)|distributions]] (i.e. generalized functions) that takes values in a ring of [[p-adic number|''p''-adic numbers]].

==Definition==
If ''X'' is a [[topological space]], a distribution on ''X'' with values in an [[abelian group]] ''G'' is a finitely additive function from the [[compact space|compact]] open subsets of ''X'' to&nbsp;''G''.  Equivalently, if we define the space of [[Distribution (mathematics)#Definitions of test functions and distributions|test functions]] to be the locally constant and compactly supported integer-valued functions, then a distribution is an additive map from  test functions to&nbsp;''G''.  This is formally similar to the usual definition of distributions, which are continuous linear maps from a space of test functions on a manifold to the real numbers.

==''p''-adic measures==
A ''p''-adic measure is a special case of a ''p''-adic distribution, analogous to a measure on a measurable space. A ''p''-adic distribution taking values in a normed space is called a ''p''-adic measure if the values on compact open subsets are bounded.
